text: {"status":"NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT","core_findings":["Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl show substantially more training-pair ranking errors (21.8% and 22.4%) than Movies_and_TV and Industrial_and_Scientific (2.3% and 1.7%). This identifies uneven training fit, not a measured validation accuracy gap.","Embedding geometry shows no obvious collapse: effective rank fractions are 0.989–0.996 with low mean pairwise cosine. Missing user panels prevent conclusions about history sensitivity."],"key_implications":["The model separates observed positives from sampled negatives less consistently in Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl.","Large margins in Movies_and_TV and Industrial_and_Scientific indicate strong sampled training separation but do not establish generalization; margin magnitudes depend on score scale.","Recommendation quality remains unassessed here because pinned validation HR@10 is unavailable."],"evidence":{"headline_metrics":{"Movies_and_TV:neg_beats_pos_rate":0.0230,"Industrial_and_Scientific:neg_beats_pos_rate":0.0167,"Electronics:neg_beats_pos_rate":0.2183,"CDs_and_Vinyl:neg_beats_pos_rate":0.2244,"Electronics:small_margin_rate":0.3350,"CDs_and_Vinyl:small_margin_rate":0.3559},"brief_metric_read":{"neg_beats_pos_rate":"Training-only sampled negatives outrank positives much more often in Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl.","small_margin_rate":"About one-third of sampled margins in these two datasets fall below 0.5; this threshold is score-scale dependent.","effective_rank_fraction":"Near-full sampled embedding rank provides no obvious evidence of collapse.","panel":"All four supplied user panels are missing; history-edit results are unavailable."}}}
